items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Wow. It almost sounds like the story I’ve heard about when Charlie Christian was introduced on the bandstand that particular night and he just was inspired to play even beyond himself.

ctx.x: Well one big thing with him was everybody had to develop their own strong sense of time, of rhythm. One thing that they’ve talked about in books and I’ve experienced this first-hand, he would rehearse the wind players without the rhythm section and sometimes he would start a tune with everybody and then cut the rhythm section out and we’d have to play on our own, swinging, as if the rhythm section was there. And I learned that that’s the way he played. He had such strong time that he could actually bring up a bad…
Wow. It almost sounds like the story I’ve heard about when Charlie Christian was introduced on the bandstand that particular night and he just was inspired to play even beyond himself.
Yeah. But that’s the thing. You know if you’re going to play music, if you’ve made this commitment, the worst thing you can do for yourself is treat it like a job and show up —
